name: Enan
title: Father of the tribal chief of Naphtali
summary: Enan is known from Numbers as the father of Ahira, who was the leader and chief of the tribe of Naphtali during the wilderness wanderings. He is mentioned mainly in connection with the census and the organization of the tribes at Sinai. Although little is known about his own life, his significance is tied to his son's role as a tribal prince.

keyEvents.title: Ahira appointed as leader of Naphtali
keyEvents.description: Enan's son Ahira was appointed chief of the tribe of Naphtali when the people of Israel were organized at Mount Sinai.

keyEvents.title: The tribe of Naphtali in the census
keyEvents.description: During the first census in the wilderness, Ahira, son of Enan, was appointed to lead the counting of the tribe of Naphtali, which numbered 53,400 men fit for battle.

keyEvents.title: Naphtali's camp and marching order
keyEvents.description: Ahira, son of Enan, was set as leader of the military division of the tribe of Naphtali in the camp on the north side of the tabernacle, under the banner of Dan.

keyEvents.title: Ahira's offering at the dedication of the altar
keyEvents.description: On the twelfth day, Ahira, son of Enan, brought his offering at the dedication of the altar in the tabernacle, as the last of the tribal princes.

keyEvents.title: Ahira leads the army of Naphtali at departure
keyEvents.description: When the people of Israel broke camp from the wilderness of Sinai, Ahira son of Enan led the division of the tribe of Naphtali as part of the rear guard.
